requirement_text: ACT or SAT scores are required.
researcher_notes: Page carries an explicit 'Updated on July 31, 2026' timestamp, within the current 2026-27 application cycle, so this is directly verified as the live, currently-operative policy for Fall 2027 entry - not a stale or historical statement. Stanford reinstated testing starting with the cycle for Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entry, cycle_year 2026) after several test-optional years during and after the pandemic; that history is corroborated by multiple secondary news sources (Stanford Daily, SF Chronicle, Crimson Education) but the original Stanford Report announcement (news.stanford.edu, June 2024) could not be directly fetched (403 Forbidden) so is NOT cited as a source here - only the live current page is. DILIGENCE CHECK for a stale test-optional page (per research brief): searched specifically for any currently-live official admission.stanford.edu or stanford.edu page still stating test-optional/not-required. Found none. The only 'test-optional' hits are third-party news articles (Stanford Daily 2021, Forbes 2021, Inside Higher Ed 2021, SF Chronicle) reporting on the since-superseded 2021-2023 policy, and the current testing.html page's own historical reference to the Class of 2029 cohort (the last test-optional class) as score-range context - neither is a live official page asserting current test-optional status. No CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE found; verdict is a clean VERIFIED_CURRENT.

requirement_text: There are no minimum test scores required to be admitted to Stanford, and there is no score that guarantees admission.
researcher_notes: Explicit disclaimer against treating any score as a threshold. Middle-50% ranges published for the Class of 2029 (ACT 34-36, SAT 1520-1570) are descriptive statistics from the last test-optional cohort, not a cutoff - should not be stored or evaluated as a minimum_grade-style scalar threshold.

requirement_text: You can enter your ACT Superscore Composite as your Highest Composite Score alongside your highest scores achieved in Math, English, and Reading across all test sittings.
researcher_notes: Self-reported superscore accepted for ACT across multiple sittings.

requirement_text: Enter your highest Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math scores
limitations: Fetched via a summarizing extraction step; the fragment shown is quoted but full original sentence boundaries were not confirmed. Re-read source directly before treating as verbatim.
researcher_notes: SAT superscore analog to the ACT policy in REQ-2026-08-21-STA0003: highest EBRW and highest Math taken across sittings, not a single-sitting total.

requirement_text: All AP exam scores must be reported if taken, even self-studied exams.
limitations: Not returned in quotation marks by the extraction step; exact original phrasing not independently confirmed.
researcher_notes: Page reportedly notes an Additional Information channel to explain any AP exam a student was unable to complete.

requirement_text: No, we do not require any English proficiency exams. If you would like to send us one, you are welcome to self-report your scores from any English proficiency exam.
researcher_notes: Stanford has NO TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo requirement or minimum score for any applicant, domestic or international - unlike most UK/European institutions researched in earlier batches, there is no test_scale/scale_ambiguity concern here because no scaled threshold is imposed at all.

requirement_text: fluency in English is a prerequisite for admission to Stanford
researcher_notes: Companion to REQ-2026-08-21-STA0006: fluency is required in substance, but Stanford does not operationalize it via a required standardized test or scale.

requirement_text: The application requirements are the same for all applicants regardless of citizenship or country of residence.
researcher_notes: Academic/essay/recommendation/testing requirements do not vary by citizenship. The genuine differences are: (a) financial aid need-awareness for non-eligible-noncitizens (see REQ-STA0011), and (b) document translation (see REQ-STA0009).

requirement_text: Yes, transcripts and teacher recommendations must be translated into English. Original copies must also be submitted when applicable. Applicants cannot translate the documents themselves.
researcher_notes: Named exclusion: self-translation by the applicant is explicitly not accepted.

requirement_text: Stanford is need-blind for all U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, undocumented students, and Eligible Noncitizens regardless of where they attend high school. This means a request for financial aid will not be a factor in our admission evaluation.
researcher_notes: Corroborated by a second, independently-worded official statement on the FAQ page (admission.stanford.edu/faqs/decision.html): 'need-blind admission policy for all U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, undocumented students and all non-U.S. citizens eligible for federal student aid.' Same substance, different phrasing, both current - not treated as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE since there is no disagreement in the underlying policy, only in wording. 'Eligible Noncitizen' functions here as domestic-equivalent status (e.g. green-card-adjacent categories), not as 'international'.

requirement_text: If you are not a U.S. citizen, legal permanent resident, undocumented student, or an Eligible Noncitizen, your request for financial aid will be a factor in our admission evaluation.
researcher_notes: DIRECT ANSWER to whether Stanford's need-blind policy extends to international applicants: it does NOT. Stanford is need-AWARE for international applicants who request financial aid - this is the opposite of need-blind, and is a genuine, confirmed, current policy difference from several domestic-equivalent peer institutions (Harvard/Princeton/Yale/MIT are commonly cited as need-blind internationally; Stanford is not - see companion agents' HAR/PRI/YAL/MIT records for cross-check, not verified independently by this lane). Directly contradicts a naive reading of REQ-2026-08-21-STA0010 in isolation - the two records must be read together.

requirement_text: We meet the full demonstrated need, without loans, for every admitted undergrad who qualifies for financial assistance.
researcher_notes: Applies once admitted and aid-eligible; does not describe the admission decision itself (see REQ-STA0010/0011 for need-blind/need-aware distinction).

requirement_text: if you apply to Stanford with a decision plan of Restrictive Early Action, you may not apply to any other private college/university under their Early Action, Restrictive Early Action, Early Decision, or Early Notification plan; and, you may not apply to any public university under an early binding plan, such as Early Decision.
researcher_notes: Companion record to the REA deadline (DL-2026-08-21-STA0001): this is the exclusivity constraint itself, verbatim, per research-brief instruction to record binding/exclusivity language as its own requirement record rather than folding it into the deadline row. This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact - should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly.

requirement_text: It is Stanford policy that you may simultaneously apply to Stanford with a decision plan of Restrictive Early Action and to any college/university with the characteristics described below: Any public college/university with an early application or early deadline plan if their decision is non-binding; Any college/university with a rolling admission process if their decision is non-binding; Any non-U.S. college/university if their decision is non-binding; Any military academy; Any college/university under Early Action or by an early deadline if the decision plan is both non-binding and applying early is required to be considered for a scholarship or special academic program.
researcher_notes: The named-exceptions carve-out to REQ-2026-08-21-STA0013 - defines the exact boundary of the REA exclusivity restriction rather than leaving it as a blanket rule. Per evidence rule 7 ('named exclusions and binding constraints invert or constrain - record explicitly'), this is recorded as its own row rather than summarized away. This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact - should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly.

requirement_text: REA applicants not admitted cannot reapply during Regular Decision that same year.
limitations: Not returned in quotation marks by the extraction step; exact original FAQ phrasing not independently re-verified word-for-word.
researcher_notes: Distinct from deferral: a student denied outright (not deferred) under REA cannot re-submit a Regular Decision application to Stanford in the same admission cycle.

requirement_text: Finalists who match to a binding institution through the National College Match are to withdraw their applications from other colleges and universities.
limitations: Paraphrase of QuestBridge program guidelines as restated on Stanford's own admission page; exact original sentence not returned in quotation marks by the extraction step.
researcher_notes: QuestBridge National College Match is a separate, binding application pathway alongside REA/RD (Stanford is one of QuestBridge's binding College Match Partners). Matched applicants must withdraw all other applications - a stronger, contractual-style commitment than REA's non-binding restriction. applies_to set to 'domestic' because QuestBridge Match is designed for students attending high school in the U.S.; this lane found no explicit Stanford-page statement excluding international citizens outright, so this scope flag is an inference from general program design, not an independently verified citizenship rule - flag for re-check against QuestBridge's own eligibility page if precision matters. This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact - should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly.

requirement_text: No, declining an interview will not incur a penalty that negatively impacts your admission decision, and you may decline for any reason. Your application will be considered complete with or without an interview.
researcher_notes: Stanford's interview is alumni-conducted and explicitly optional with no scoring/completeness penalty for opting out or not being offered one.

requirement_text: Interview capacity is limited by alumni availability. Many applicants do not receive interview invitations.
researcher_notes: Availability-gated, not applicant-controlled - a student should not be told to 'go request an interview'; Stanford extends invitations by alumni availability in the applicant's high school area.

researcher_notes: Fee waiver: Stanford accepts the Common App fee waiver for all eligible students, U.S. and non-U.S. Applicants need not wait for waiver approval before submitting.

requirement_text: Applicants are limited to a total of three applications for undergraduate admission, whether for first-year admission, transfer admission or a combination of both.
researcher_notes: Lifetime/cumulative cap across first-year and transfer attempts combined, not a per-cycle limit.
